za-dynasty.s: The Za dynasty was an early ruling dynasty of the Songhai people, centred on Gao in the bend of the Niger River. The Songhai Empire profile notes that a Songhai kingdom under the Za dynasty existed for generations as a tributary state within the Mali Empire.

zabt-system.s: The zabt system was a method of land revenue assessment in the Mughal Empire, developed under Akbar and associated with his minister Todar Mal. Land was measured and classified, and the tax was fixed in cash on the basis of average yields and prices over several years.

zacatecas.s: Zacatecas is a city in north-central Mexico founded after the discovery of rich silver deposits in 1546. It became one of the most productive silver-mining centres of New Spain.

zafarnama.s: The Zafarnama, or Book of Victory, is a Persian chronicle of the life and conquests of Timur, written under Timurid patronage. Versions were composed by Nizam al-Din Shami and later by Sharaf al-Din Ali Yazdi.

zaghawa.s: The Zaghawa are a people of the eastern Sahara and Sahel, living in present-day Chad and Sudan. Early Arabic writers used the name for the rulers and people of the region around Lake Chad.

zagros-mountains.s: The Zagros Mountains are a long mountain range in western Iran, stretching from the borders of Turkey to the Persian Gulf and separating the Mesopotamian plain from the Iranian plateau. Their highland peoples repeatedly pressed on Mesopotamian states, including the Akkadian…

zagwe-dynasty.s: The Zagwe dynasty was a ruling dynasty of the northern Ethiopian highlands that rose to power after the decline of Aksum, from around 940 CE according to the site's chronology. It is best known for the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela, built under its king of that name.

zaju.s: Zaju is a form of Chinese drama combining spoken dialogue, song and music, which reached its classical form under the Yuan Dynasty. Its four-act plays treated historical, romantic and moral themes.

zakat.s: Zakat is the obligatory almsgiving of Islam, one of the Five Pillars, levied as a proportion of certain kinds of wealth and distributed to the poor and other specified recipients. In Islamic states it also functioned as a tax.

zaman-shah-durrani.s: Zaman Shah Durrani was ruler of the Durrani Empire of Afghanistan in the 1790s, a grandson of Ahmad Shah Durrani. He launched several invasions of the Punjab.

zambezi.s: The Zambezi is the fourth-longest river in Africa, flowing from Zambia through Angola, along the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe, and across Mozambique to the Indian Ocean. It was a major route for trade between the interior and the coast.

zambia.s: Zambia is a landlocked country in south-central Africa, including part of the Central African Copperbelt. The Lunda Empire profile places the empire's origins in a region spanning the south-east of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Angola and parts of…

zanata-berbers.s: The Zanata were one of the major Berber confederations of North Africa, many of them pastoral nomads of the Maghreb and the northern Sahara. They played a large role in the politics of the medieval Maghreb, later founding the Marinid and Zayyanid dynasties.

zand-dynasty.s: The Zand dynasty ruled much of Iran from about 1751 to 1794, founded by Karim Khan Zand, a chief of the Zand tribe of the Zagros. Karim Khan governed from Shiraz under the title of Vakil, bringing a period of relative peace after the collapse of the Afsharid Empire.

zanj-rebellion.s: The Zanj Rebellion was a major revolt in southern Iraq from 869 to 883, led by Ali ibn Muhammad and involving enslaved East Africans, known as the Zanj, who laboured in the salt marshes near Basra. The rebels established a state, sacked Basra and defeated Abbasid armies for…

zara-yaqob.s: Zara Yaqob was Emperor of Ethiopia from 1434 to 1468, one of the most powerful rulers of the Solomonic dynasty. He centralised royal authority, reformed the Ethiopian Church and promoted religious literature.

zaragoza.s: Zaragoza is a city in north-eastern Spain on the Ebro River, in the medieval period the capital of an important taifa kingdom of al-Andalus. It was the most important Almoravid city in north-eastern Spain.

zaria.s: Zaria is a city in northern Nigeria, historically the capital of the Hausa state of Zazzau. It became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate after the jihad of the early nineteenth century.

zarpanitu.s: Zarpanitu was a Babylonian goddess, the consort of Marduk, the chief god of Babylon. Her statue stood with his in the Esagila temple.

zayyanid-dynasty.s: The Zayyanid dynasty was a Berber dynasty that ruled the central Maghreb from Tlemcen, in present-day Algeria, from the thirteenth to the sixteenth century. Of Zanata origin, it emerged from the fragmentation of the Almohad Caliphate.

zeila.s: Zeila is a port town on the Gulf of Aden coast in present-day Somaliland, historically a major outlet for trade between the Ethiopian highlands and the Red Sea and Indian Ocean. The Adal Sultanate profile records that Sabr ad-Din III reconstituted the Walashma state at Zeila…

zemene-mesafint.s: The Zemene Mesafint, or Era of the Princes, was a period of Ethiopian history from 1769 until the mid-nineteenth century, in which the emperors were largely powerless and regional lords held real authority. The Ethiopian Empire profile notes that many emperors occupied the…

zeng-guofan.s: Zeng Guofan was a Chinese scholar-official and military leader who raised and commanded the Xiang Army, which played a central role in suppressing the Taiping Rebellion. He was also a leading figure in the Self-Strengthening Movement.

zengid-dynasty.s: The Zengid dynasty was a Turkic dynasty that ruled northern Iraq and Syria in the twelfth century, founded by Imad al-Din Zengi, who captured Edessa from the Crusaders in 1144. His son Nur al-Din extended Zengid power and sent forces into Fatimid Egypt.

zerafshan.s: The Zerafshan is a river of Central Asia that flows west from the mountains of Tajikistan through Uzbekistan, watering the oases of Samarkand and Bukhara. Its valley was one of the richest agricultural and commercial regions of Transoxiana.

zheng-family.s: The Zheng family was a maritime trading and military clan of south-eastern China, led by Zheng Zhilong and his son Zheng Chenggong, known in the West as Koxinga. Remaining loyal to the Ming, they resisted the Qing conquest and in 1662 seized Taiwan from the Dutch.

zheng-he.s: Zheng He was a Chinese admiral and court eunuch who led seven great maritime expeditions for the Ming Empire between 1405 and 1433. His fleets of large treasure ships sailed through Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean as far as Arabia and East Africa, establishing tributary…

zhizhi.s: Zhizhi was a Xiongnu chanyu of the first century BCE, a brother and rival of Huhanye during the civil war that split the Xiongnu Empire. While Huhanye submitted to the Han Dynasty, Zhizhi led his followers westward.

zhu-wen.s: Zhu Wen was a Chinese military leader who first fought as a rebel under Huang Chao and then served the Tang Dynasty before turning against it. The Tang Dynasty profile records that in 907 he forced the last Tang emperor to abdicate and founded the Later Liang dynasty.

zhu-xi.s: Zhu Xi was a Chinese philosopher of the Southern Song Dynasty and the leading figure of Neo-Confucianism. His synthesis of Confucian ethics and metaphysics, and his commentaries on the Four Books, later became the basis of the imperial civil service examinations.

ziggurat.s: A ziggurat is a massive stepped temple tower built in ancient Mesopotamia and Elam, with a shrine on its summit. Ziggurats were constructed of mud brick, often faced with baked brick, and served as the centre of a city's religious life.

ziggurat-of-ur.s: The Ziggurat of Ur is a great stepped temple tower at the ancient city of Ur in southern Iraq, dedicated to the moon god Nanna. It was built by Ur-Nammu and completed by his son Shulgi in the twenty-first century BCE.

zimbabwe.s: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa, whose name derives from the stone enclosures of Great Zimbabwe. Its plateau was home to a succession of states built on gold, cattle and trade, including the Mutapa Empire and the Rozvi Empire.

zimbabwean-plateau.s: The Zimbabwean plateau is a high plateau in southern Africa between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers, rich in gold and suited to cattle herding. It was the setting of Great Zimbabwe and later of the Mutapa and Rozvi states.

zimri-lim.s: Zimri-Lim was the last king of Mari, a city-state on the middle Euphrates in present-day Syria, in the eighteenth century BCE. His palace archive is a major source for the period.

zinkekra.s: Zinkekra is an archaeological site in the Fezzan region of south-western Libya, a fortified hilltop settlement above the Wadi al-Ajal. The Garamantian Empire profile identifies the citadel at Zinkekra as the royal centre of the Garamantes during their formative phase.

zionism.s: Zionism is the nationalist movement that emerged in the late nineteenth century to establish a Jewish national homeland in Palestine. Its political form was founded by Theodor Herzl, whose writings and organisation of the first Zionist Congress in 1897 gave it international…

zirid-dynasty.s: The Zirid dynasty was a Sanhaja Berber dynasty that governed Ifriqiya, roughly present-day Tunisia and eastern Algeria, on behalf of the Fatimid Caliphate after the Fatimids moved to Egypt. The Fatimid Caliphate profile records that between about 1048 and 1052 the Zirid…

zliten-mosaic.s: The Zliten Mosaic is a Roman floor mosaic found at a villa at Zliten, near Leptis Magna in Libya, depicting gladiatorial combat and the killing of prisoners by wild animals in the arena. The Garamantian Empire profile notes that it shows lions and leopards supplied by the…

zoroastrianism.s: Zoroastrianism is an ancient Iranian religion founded on the teachings of the prophet Zoroaster, centred on the worship of Ahura Mazda and the struggle between good and evil. It was the state religion of the Sasanian Empire, whose kings drew legitimacy from it.

zoskales.s: Zoskales was a king associated with Aksum in the first century CE, the earliest Aksumite ruler named in a written source. The Aksumite Empire profile notes that the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea describes him as Greek-educated.

zubayrids.s: The Zubayrids were the supporters of Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who claimed the caliphate from Mecca during the Second Fitna after the death of Yazid I in 683. For several years they controlled much of the Islamic world.

zulu-kingdom.s: The Zulu Kingdom was a powerful state in south-eastern Africa built by Shaka from the 1810s onward through military reform and conquest. Its rise was associated with the Mfecane, a period of warfare and migration that spread across southern Africa.

zumbo.s: Zumbo was a trading settlement on the Zambezi River, in present-day Mozambique near the borders of Zambia and Zimbabwe. The Rozvi Empire profile notes that gold exports were channelled through coastal trading fairs at Zumbo and Masekesa.

zwangendaba.s: Zwangendaba was a Nguni military leader who led the Ngoni people northwards from south-eastern Africa during the upheavals of the Mfecane in the early nineteenth century. The Rozvi Empire profile records that Zwangendaba's Ngoni crossed the Zimbabwean plateau from…

zhang-er.s: Zhang Er was a statesman from the former state of Wei who joined the revolt against the Qin and helped restore the kingdom of Zhao. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made him King of Changshan, but his former friend Chen Yu drove him out with help from Qi, and he joined Liu Bang.

zhang-han.s: Zhang Han was the last great general of the Qin dynasty. He crushed Chen Sheng's rebellion and defeated Xiang Liang, but after the Qin defeat at Julu he surrendered to Xiang Yu in 207 BCE.

zang-tu.s: Zang Tu was a general of the revived state of Yan who followed Xiang Yu against the Qin. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu made him King of Yan, and he killed his former lord Han Guang to take Liaodong as well.

zhao-shanzheng.s: Zhao Shanzheng was a figurehead ruler of the short-lived Da Tianxing kingdom in Yunnan. After the official Yang Ganzhen had the last Da Changhe ruler killed in 928, he placed Zhao on the throne at Yangjumie.

zhao-xie.s: Zhao Xie was a descendant of the old royal house of Zhao, restored as its king during the revolts against the Qin dynasty. In 206 BCE Xiang Yu moved him north to the Kingdom of Dai, giving Zhao to Zhang Er.

zog-i.s: Zog I, born Ahmet Zogu, was an Albanian chieftain from Mat who dominated his country's politics between the wars. He overthrew Fan Noli's government in December 1924, became president of the Albanian Republic in 1925 and proclaimed himself King of the Albanians in 1928.

zhai-zhao.s: Zhai Zhao was the second and last ruler of Zhai Wei, a small Dingling state on the Yellow River during the Sixteen Kingdoms period. He succeeded his father Zhai Liao in 391, but in 392 Murong Chui of the Later Yan forced the river crossing and took his capital Huatai.

zhang-qian.s: Zhang Qian was a Han dynasty envoy sent west by Emperor Wu around 138 BCE to seek an alliance with the Yuezhi against the Xiongnu. Held captive by the Xiongnu for years, he reached Dayuan, Kangju and Bactria and returned in 126 BCE; a later mission went to the Wusun.

zalim-singh-jhala.s: Zalim Singh Jhala was the regent and real ruler of Kota in Rajasthan from the 1770s until his death in 1824. A capable administrator and soldier, he reformed the revenue, kept Kota safe from Maratha and Pindari raids and allied with the British in 1817.

zaporozhian-cossacks.s: The Zaporozhian Cossacks were the Cossacks of the lower Dnieper, organised from the 16th century around the fortified Zaporozhian Sich beyond the river's rapids. Under Bohdan Khmelnytsky they led the rising of 1648 against Poland-Lithuania that created the Cossack Hetmanate.

zayed-bin-sultan-al-nahyan.s: Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan was ruler of Abu Dhabi from 1966, when he replaced his brother Shakhbut, and used its new oil revenues for rapid development. With Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum of Dubai he led the talks among the Trucial States that created the United Arab Emirates in…

zhai-liao.s: Zhai Liao was a Dingling chieftain who founded the Zhai Wei state on the Yellow River in Henan during the break-up of the Former Qin. After serving and turning on several powers in turn, he proclaimed himself Heavenly King of Wei in 388.

zhang-bangchang.s: Zhang Bangchang was a Song dynasty chancellor installed by the Jurchen Jin as emperor of the puppet state of Da Chu at Kaifeng in 1127, after they captured the city and deported the Song emperors Huizong and Qinzong. He held the throne for about a month, then handed power back…

zhang-shicheng.s: Zhang Shicheng was a salt-boat worker who rose in revolt against the Yuan dynasty in 1353 and set up the state of Zhou, ruling the rich Yangtze delta from Suzhou. He wavered between rebellion and Yuan allegiance, and his troops killed the Red Turban leader Liu Futong in 1363.

zhang-xianzhong.s: Zhang Xianzhong was a peasant rebel leader of the late Ming dynasty. After years of campaigning across northern and central China, he took Chengdu in 1644 and proclaimed the Great Xi state in Sichuan.

zhang-zuolin.s: Zhang Zuolin was a Chinese warlord who rose from bandit leader to master of Manchuria as head of the Fengtian clique. During the Beiyang period he fought the Zhili clique for control of Beijing and from 1927 headed the Beiyang government himself.

zhao-tuo.s: Zhao Tuo was a Qin general sent to conquer the far south who founded the kingdom of Nanyue, with its capital at Panyu (Guangzhou), in 204 BCE. Ruling Chinese settlers and Yue peoples, he adopted local customs, accepted Han overlordship in 196 BCE and later styled himself emperor.

zheng-jing.s: Zheng Jing was the son of Koxinga and ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning on Taiwan from 1662 to 1681. With his minister Chen Yonghua he built a Chinese-style administration at Tungning (Tainan), founding Taiwan's first Confucian temple and encouraging foreign trade.

zheng-keshuang.s: Zheng Keshuang was the last ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning on Taiwan and a grandson of Koxinga. Court factions placed him on the throne as a boy after his father Zheng Jing died in 1681.

zheng-longdan.s: Zheng Longdan was the last king of Da Changhe, the Zheng family's kingdom in Yunnan that had replaced Nanzhao in 902. He came to the throne young in 926, while rivalry among the great families of the Erhai region weakened the court.

zheng-maisi.s: Zheng Maisi was a minister of Nanzhao, descended from a Tang official captured by the kingdom. In 902 he massacred the Meng royal family and proclaimed the kingdom of Da Changhe, centred on the Erhai basin of Yunnan.

zhenzhu-khagan.s: Zhenzhu Khagan, personal name Yinan, was the leader of the Xueyantuo, a Tiele people of Mongolia. He led their revolt against the Eastern Turkic Khaganate in 628 and was recognised as khagan by Emperor Taizong of Tang.

zhingshak-tseten-dorje.s: Zhingshak Tseten Dorje, also called Karma Tseten, was the founder of the Tsangpa dynasty of Tibet. An official of the Rinpungpa at Samdrubtse (Shigatse), he rebelled in the 1550s and by 1565 had replaced his masters as ruler of Tsang.

zhu-youzhen.s: Zhu Youzhen was the last emperor of the Later Liang dynasty in northern China, a son of its founder Zhu Wen. In 913 he overthrew his brother Zhu Yougui, who had murdered their father.

ziri-ibn-atiyya.s: Ziri ibn Atiyya was a chief of the Maghrawa, a Zenata Berber tribe, and an ally of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba against the Fatimids. Around 987 he took control of Fez as Córdoba's governor, and in 994 he founded Oujda.

zviad-gamsakhurdia.s: Zviad Gamsakhurdia was a Georgian dissident writer and nationalist leader who became the first elected president of Georgia. His coalition won the Soviet Georgian elections of 1990, and Georgia declared independence on 9 April 1991, with him elected president the following month.

zeki-velidi-togan.s: Zeki Velidi Togan, born Akhmetzaki Validov, was a Bashkir national leader and historian. In 1917 to 1920 he led the government of autonomous Bashkurdistan, negotiating between the Whites and the Bolsheviks before breaking with Soviet power and joining the Basmachi in Central…

zainal-abidin-of-ternate.s: Zainal Abidin of Ternate was ruler of Ternate in the Maluku Islands in the late fifteenth century. He studied Islam at Giri in eastern Java and is credited with formally adopting Islam and taking the title of sultan, making Ternate the first Islamic sultanate of the Moluccas.

zainal-abidin-i-of-terengganu.s: Zainal Abidin I of Terengganu was the founder of the present Terengganu Sultanate on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula. A son of the Bendahara family of the Johor Sultanate, he became sultan around 1708, and his descendants still rule Terengganu as a state of Malaysia.

zahir-al-umar.s: Zahir al-Umar was an Arab sheikh of the Zaydani clan who built an autonomous domain in Galilee in the 18th century, taking Tiberias and making Acre his capital and a busy cotton-exporting port. He defied the Ottoman governors of Damascus and allied with Ali Bey of Egypt and…

zain-ul-abidin.s: Zain-ul-Abidin, called Budshah, the great king, was sultan of Kashmir from 1418 to 1470 in the Shah Mir dynasty. He reversed his father Sikandar's persecution, allowed Hindu Pandits to return, had Sanskrit works translated into Persian and patronised crafts.

zakhary-chepiha.s: Zakhary Chepiha was a Cossack commander who led the Black Sea Cossack Host formed from former Zaporozhians. He fought in the Russo-Turkish War of 1787 to 1792, including the capture of Izmail.

zakkur.s: Zakkur was an Aramaean king of Hamath and Lu'ash around 800 BCE, probably a usurper. His Aramaic stele, found at Tell Afis, ancient Hatarikka, records how the god Baalshamin saved him when a coalition of kings led by Bar-Hadad of Aram-Damascus besieged him there.

zanticus.s: Zanticus was a king of the Iazyges, a Sarmatian people of the Hungarian plain, during the Marcomannic Wars. After the Romans defeated his people, he made peace with Marcus Aurelius in 175, returning tens of thousands of Roman captives and providing 8,000 cavalry, of whom 5,500…

zasagt-khan.s: Zasagt Khan was the title of the Chinggisid rulers of the western Khalkha Mongols, one of the three, later four, Khalkha khanates. The title was adopted in the late 16th century by a branch of Geresenje's descendants ruling towards the Khangai and Altai mountains.

zawi-ibn-ziri.s: Zawi ibn Ziri was a Sanhaja Berber leader of the Zirid family who came to al-Andalus to serve the Caliphate of Córdoba. During the civil war after 1009 he seized the district of Elvira around 1013 and moved its centre to Granada, founding the Taifa of Granada.

zayed-bin-khalifa-al-nahyan.s: Zayed bin Khalifa Al Nahyan, known as Zayed the Great, was ruler of Abu Dhabi from 1855 to 1909. Through war and alliances with inland tribes he made Abu Dhabi the strongest of the Trucial States, and he signed the Exclusive Agreement with Britain in 1892.

zayyan-ibn-mardanish.s: Zayyan ibn Mardanish was the last Muslim ruler of Valencia, a descendant of Muhammad ibn Mardanish, the Wolf King. In 1229 he overthrew the Almohad governor Abu Zayd and took Valencia, but James I of Aragon conquered the kingdom, winning at Puig in 1237 and taking the city…

zenobia.s: Zenobia was queen of Palmyra, who ruled for her young son Vaballathus after the murder of her husband Odaenathus in 267. She conquered Egypt in 270 and much of Anatolia, creating a breakaway Palmyrene Empire in Rome's East.

zeus-polieus.s: Zeus Polieus, Zeus of the city, was a form of the Greek god Zeus worshipped as protector of a city and its citizens. His cult was often shared with Athena Polias on the acropolis, as at Athens, where the Dipolieia festival honoured him.

zhang-fu-ming-general.s: Zhang Fu was a Ming general who served in the 1406 to 1407 invasion of Vietnam that overthrew the Ho dynasty and created Jiaozhi province. He returned several times to crush resistance, capturing the Later Tran rulers Gian Dinh in 1409 and Trung Quang in 1414.

zhang-gui.s: Zhang Gui was a Chinese official appointed governor of Liang province in the far north-west by the Western Jin in 301. Ruling from Guzang, he restored order, encouraged learning and welcomed refugees from the wars in northern China.

zhang-jun-former-liang.s: Zhang Jun was ruler of Former Liang from 324 to 346, a grandson of its founder Zhang Gui. Under him the state reached its greatest extent, controlling the Hexi Corridor and influence in the Western Regions, and in 327 he established Gaochang commandery in the Turpan basin.

zhang-tianxi.s: Zhang Tianxi was the last ruler of Former Liang, who seized power in 363. In 376 the Former Qin ruler Fu Jian invaded, and Zhang Tianxi surrendered and served at the Qin court.

zhang-yichao.s: Zhang Yichao was a local leader of Dunhuang who in 848 drove out the Tibetan garrison as the Tibetan Empire disintegrated, and went on to free other towns of the Hexi Corridor. The Tang court recognised him in 851 as military governor of the Guiyi Circuit.

zhao-mo.s: Zhao Mo was the second king of Nanyue, grandson of its founder Zhao Tuo, reigning from 137 BCE. He relied on the Han dynasty for help against Minyue.

zhao-xiangzi.s: Zhao Xiangzi was head of the Zhao lineage, ministers of the State of Jin, in the 5th century BCE. Around 457 BCE he killed the king of Dai at a banquet and annexed his state.

zhelyu-zhelev.s: Zhelyu Zhelev was a Bulgarian philosopher and dissident whose book on fascism was banned under communism. He led the opposition Union of Democratic Forces in 1989 and 1990, was elected president by parliament in 1990 and became the first directly elected president of Bulgaria…

zhu-yougui.s: Zhu Yougui was the second emperor of the Later Liang in the Five Dynasties period. In 912 he murdered his father Zhu Wen, the dynasty's founder, and took the throne.

zhuge-liang.s: Zhuge Liang was the chancellor of Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms period and chief adviser to Liu Bei, whose alliance with Sun Quan led to victory at Red Cliffs in 208. After Liu Bei's death he governed for Liu Shan, pacified the south and led five northern expeditions against…

ziaur-rahman.s: Ziaur Rahman was a Bangladeshi army officer who announced the declaration of independence on radio in March 1971 and commanded forces in the Liberation War. After the coups of 1975 he became the country's leading figure and was president from 1977.

zmitser-zhylunovich.s: Zmitser Zhylunovich was a Belarusian writer, known by the pen name Tsishka Hartny, and head of the provisional government of the Socialist Soviet Republic of Byelorussia proclaimed in January 1919. He broke with the Bolsheviks when the republic was merged into the…

zorawar-singh.s: Zorawar Singh was a Dogra general in the service of Gulab Singh of Jammu. Between 1834 and 1840 he conquered Ladakh and Baltistan, bringing them into the Dogra realm that later became the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.

zou-yao.s: Zou Yao was a descendant of King Goujian of Yue who helped the Han against Xiang Yu. In 192 BCE Emperor Hui of Han made him King of Donghai, ruling from Dong'ou in southern Zhejiang.

zulfikar-ali-bhutto.s: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was a Pakistani statesman who founded the Pakistan Peoples Party in 1967. After the loss of East Pakistan in 1971 he became president and then prime minister, nationalised industries, introduced the 1973 constitution and began Pakistan's nuclear programme.
